Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the web search results, I found several clear, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting the burden of AI-generated submissions.

Here are the key examples, with the required citation format following each.

**curl:**
The curl project, maintained by Daniel Stenberg, is a primary example. Stenberg has been vocal about the issue, leading to the project adding an AI disclosure checkbox to its HackerOne bug bounty program and eventually shutting the program down.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg equated the time wasted on invalid AI-generated reports to a DDoS attack.

SOURCE: https://www.axios.com/2026/03/10/ai-agents-spam-the-volunteers-securing-open-source-software | QUOTE: ""The never-ending slop submissions take a serious mental toll to manage and sometimes also a long time to debunk," Stenberg wrote. "Time and energy that is completely wasted while also hampering our will to live."" | CLAIM: Stenberg stated that AI "slop" submissions cause a serious mental toll and waste time, hampering the maintainers' "will to live."

**Python:**
The search results indicate that Seth Larson, a Python security developer, also raised concerns about the burden of these reports.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Python's Seth Larson also raised concerns about these AI slop reports back in December, saying that responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: Seth Larson stated that responding to AI slop reports is expensive and time-consuming because they appear legitimate and require investigation.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: ""Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports," Larson wrote. "All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson wrote that time-wasting security reports lead to negative emotions and contribute to maintainer burnout.

**Ghostty:**
Mitchell Hashimoto, a maintainer of the Ghostty terminal emulator, publicly discussed the issue on social media and changed the project's policy.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "> It’s a fucking war zone out here man. Maintainer morale at an all time low. I totally empathize with the projects that flip the table and ban all AI. I’m getting close to saying only maintainers and accepted issues can have any AI . — Mitchell Hashimoto (@mitchellh) January 16, 2026" | CLAIM: Mitchell Hashimoto described the situation as a "war zone" with maintainer morale at an all-time low due to AI slop.

**tldraw:**
Steve Ruiz, founder of tldraw, implemented a policy to auto-close external pull requests after being overwhelmed.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "Ruiz’s response was the most drastic: tldraw now auto-closes all external pull requests, full stop." | CLAIM: Steve Ruiz's project, tldraw, implemented a policy to auto-close all external pull requests in response to the problem.

**RubyGems:**
The package manager for Ruby is also considering changes due to the volume of invalid reports.

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "RubyGems, the package manager for the Ruby programming language, is mulling a similar move because it hasn’t seen a valid report in months, said Marty Haught, director of open source at Ruby Central." | CLAIM: RubyGems is considering closing its bug bounty program because it has not seen a valid security report in months due to the influx of AI slop.

**General Trend:**
The sources also document the scale of the problem for maintainers in general.

SOURCE: https://www.axios.com/2026/03/10/ai-agents-spam-the-volunteers-securing-open-source-software | QUOTE: "On average, a popular open-source project would get two or three bug reports in a week to review, Robinson estimated. Less popular projects received one report a month. - Now, some projects are getting hundreds of reports at one time, he added." | CLAIM: An expert estimated that some open-source projects are now receiving hundreds of AI-generated reports at a time, up from just a few per week or month.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: I could not find a direct link to the original Mastodon post by Daniel Stenberg mentioned in one of the search result snippets. The provided link is to a Mastodon instance, but the snippet does not contain a quotable statement about the burden. The other sources provide sufficient documentation of his statements.
